text:
Maize dwarf mosaic (a mosaic virus).

Symptoms: leaves show a mottled light-and-dark green patchy (mosaic) pattern, along with stunted growth; infected plants may also show excessive tillering/branching and significantly reduced yield, especially when infection occurs early in the plant's life.

Management: because this virus is spread mainly by aphids, controlling the aphid vector is a key management strategy. Managing weeds -- particularly Johnson grass, which can act as an alternate host/reservoir for the virus between seasons -- helps reduce the source of infection. Removing infected plants early can help limit further spread within a field, and some resistant varieties are available.
